findings.observed: 'Fourth — and anticipating the rest of the book — even at 3000 examples the model is still surface-fragile on the reworded test we ran.' No reworded/surface test exists for the data-scaling experiment: scripts/run_data_scaling.py evaluates in-distribution pass@1 only (grep for surface/reword/wording/held_word returns nothing), artifacts/manifests/data_scaling.json has only {dataset_size, final_loss, pass_at_1, train_time_s}, and docs/experiments/data_scaling.md reports only in-distribution pass@1. The same chapter states it 'measured familiar-task performance only' (line 60) and that surface/composition are separate questions it did not measure.
findings.evidence: run_data_scaling.py:66 res = evaluate_all(m, tok, train, pool_test, judge) with pool_test built from a fresh letters-id-set pool; no surface split is constructed. data_scaling.json rows contain no surface field. docs/experiments/data_scaling.md result table has one score column.
findings.why_it_matters: This claims measured capability (surface fragility of the 3000-example model) that no experiment produced — the anti-fabrication bedrock of review §4.1 — and it directly contradicts the chapter's own honest scoping two paragraphs earlier.
findings.required_correction: Delete the clause or replace it with a sourced statement explicitly attributed to the Stage-3 surface run (stage3_surface: held-out wording 0.000 over 600 records), making clear the data-scaled models were never evaluated on a reworded surface.
findings.acceptance_test: grep ch11 for 'surface-fragile' returns either nothing or a sentence naming the stage3_surface run as the source; no surface/reworded score is attributed to any data_scaling size point.

findings.observed: ch17 asserts 'We built a small equivalence check and confirmed it matched on the bounded integer domain we enumerated', and Appendix C says the 6 survivors were 'all six verified equivalent ... over the integer domain'. docs/experiments/judge_mutation.md:52-53 states the opposite: 'We did not build an equivalence check, so we report "survived" plainly rather than guess which are truly equivalent.' artifacts/manifests/judge_mutation.json contains only {aggregate, per_operation} kill counts — no equivalence field — and no equivalence-check implementation exists anywhere in scripts/, src/, or tests/ (run_mutation_report.py has only aspirational comments and fake_sibling() that returns the source unchanged).
findings.evidence: judge_mutation.json keys = ['aggregate','per_operation']; grep -rn -i equivalen over scripts/src/tests/docs hits only run_mutation_report.py comments, live_demo.py, and the contradicting docs sentence.
findings.why_it_matters: An asserted executed verification with no artifact, contradicting the book's own experiment record; the equivalence-adjusted mutation score 29/29 = 1.000 presented in ch17 rests on it. In a book whose credibility rests on measured provenance this is a fabrication-class defect.
findings.required_correction: Reconcile one way: (a) commit the equivalence check and record its output in judge_mutation.json, cite it in ch17/Appendix C, and update docs/experiments/judge_mutation.md; or (b) rewrite ch17/Appendix C to present equivalence as a mathematical case analysis only ([DERIVED], no claim of a built-and-run check), label the 1.000 adjusted score as derived from that analysis, and keep the doc's wording.
findings.acceptance_test: ch17 contains no claim of an executed equivalence check unless a cited script+output artifact exists; book, docs, and manifest state identical provenance for the six survivors.

findings.observed: ch21 repeatedly extends the parsing-failure cause to every composition run and all four sizes ('the held-out composite ... was 0.000 in every composition run, and those held-out candidates failed parsing (Appendix B.10)'; 'held-out at 0.88M, 6.5M, 10.2M, and 29.3M — though, as Chapter 16 notes, the held-out composites all failed parsing'). ch16 explicitly scopes the claim the other way: it is about 'the composition-exposure run' and says 'we do not extend that parsing finding to other size checkpoints, whose recorded stage rates we did not analyze the same way.' Appendix B.10 analyzed only the composition_exposure run. Moreover the only surviving 0.88M composition eval, artifacts/manifests/stage4_scaling.json (ckpt stage1.pt), records compositional syntax_rate = 0.1833 (11/60 parsed), i.e. the 0.88M held-out candidates did NOT all fail parsing.
findings.evidence: stage4_scaling.json compositional MODEL: syntax_rate 0.1833, executable 0.0, pass_at_1 0.0; stage4_composition_{6p5m,10m}.json and stage4_composition.json record compositional syntax_rate 0.0; composition_exposure_pilot.json held_out syntax_rate 0.0; composition_diversity_pilot.json records no syntax rates at all.
findings.why_it_matters: ch21 states as fact a cause that ch16 explicitly declined to generalize, and that the 0.88M manifest contradicts — turning an unresolved, run-scoped cause into a universal explanation of the canonical 0.000 across the capacity grid.
findings.required_correction: Scope every 'failed parsing' statement to the runs whose manifests record syntax_rate 0.0 (exposure run; 6.5M/10.2M/29.3M), state that the 0.88M baseline eval parsed 0.183 of held-out candidates (stage4_scaling.json) so its zero has a different recorded profile, and remove the false 'as Chapter 16 notes' attribution in ch21.
findings.acceptance_test: No sentence claims all held-out candidates failed parsing for the 0.88M baseline or for the diversity run; each parsing claim cites a manifest whose compositional syntax_rate is 0.0, and ch21's wording matches ch16's scoping.

findings.location: book/manuscript/ch25_conclusion.md:39-41 and book/manuscript/appendix_b_failure_ledger.md:97-107 (entry 6); same collapse in docs/experiments/human_test_set.md
findings.observed: Both passages use the aggregate '0/16' as confirmation of the surface (Level-3) finding — ch25: 'The external reality check confirmed it: a human-written test set scored 0/16, because the model learned a template, not the task'; Appendix B.6: 'This is the external, real-world corroboration of the surface finding.' But 5 of the 16 requests (12-16) are genuinely held-out composites, i.e. Level-4 structural evidence whose failure is expected for a different reason. Only ch15:207-211 decomposes the number correctly: 0 of 11 seen-operation requests (surface) and 0 of 5 held-out composite requests (structural).
findings.evidence: ch15:193-211 gives the per-request mapping and the 0/11 + 0/5 split; docs/experiments/human_test_set.md concedes 'The model was also never trained on composite ops (they're held out), so those failing is expected and separate.'
findings.why_it_matters: This collapses Level-3 and Level-4 evidence into one number supporting one claim — precisely the collapse the book's central four-level taxonomy forbids ('never mash these four into one number', ch02:76) — in the conclusion and the failure ledger, the two places readers quote from.
findings.required_correction: Wherever 0/16 is cited as evidence, give the decomposition (0/11 surface-phrasing failures = Q3; 0/5 held-out composites = Q4, expected separately) or explicitly state the aggregate mixes two generalization levels; apply the same fix to Appendix B.6 and docs/experiments/human_test_set.md.
findings.acceptance_test: ch25 and Appendix B.6 each show 0/11 and 0/5 (or an explicit 'this aggregate mixes Q3 and Q4' note) before using 0/16 as corroboration.

findings.observed: ch12 states the causal story as settled fact: the retrain ran 'avoiding the CPU-dispatch crash that had interrupted the original training', 'the original training hit a hardware-level SIGILL twice', and 'the earlier 0.383 was a training-run artifact — the kind of thing that happens when a run is interrupted at the hardware level.' docs/experiments/scaling_composition.md explicitly hedges: 'The 0.383 "bigger is worse" anomaly was almost certainly a training-run artifact, not a reproducible property' and 'The original checkpoint was not preserved, so we cannot forensically confirm the crash.' ch22 ('turned out to be a training-run artifact') and ch25 ('not the earlier 0.383 artifact') repeat the unhedged version.
findings.evidence: docs/experiments/scaling_composition.md lines 59-74 vs ch12:153-163; no manifest preserves the original 10M run (original checkpoint not preserved per the doc).
findings.why_it_matters: An [INTERPRETATION]/hypothesis about an unpreserved checkpoint is presented as a measured causal finding, and the book's own experiment record says the crash's role cannot be forensically confirmed — an overclaimed label on one of the four canonical grid values.
findings.required_correction: Restore the hedge in ch12, ch22 and ch25: keep 0.773 as the measured clean-retrain value, but label the 'crash caused the 0.383' attribution as interpretation ('almost certainly', original checkpoint not preserved, crash role unconfirmed), matching docs/experiments/scaling_composition.md.
findings.acceptance_test: No sentence in ch12/ch22/ch25 asserts the SIGILL caused the 0.383 without the unconfirmed-forensics caveat; wording matches the experiment doc's certainty level.

findings.observed: The canonical NOT-tested list covers seeds, diversity-run families, isolated rungs, >30M composition, replay-after-A-first, and mutation coverage — but omits the ability-ladder stages 5-6 that review §4.2 requires: increased Python expressivity beyond the tested operations, longer/more-complex programs, and other generalization axes outside the four questions. A full-manuscript grep for 'expressiv|longer program|greater complex|complex program|ability ladder' returns zero hits: program length/complexity is never named as untested anywhere. ch25's future note covers 'more Python (loops, indexing, richer structures)' but not length/complexity, and ch22's syntax inventory covers only isolated rungs.
findings.evidence: grep over book/manuscript/*.md for expressivity/length/complexity terms: 0 matches; Appendix C NOT-tested list enumerated at lines 277-307.
findings.why_it_matters: Review §4 names this the book's recurring omission class: the tested vs untested Python-capability surface must be stated explicitly, not implied complete. The conclusion gestures at it but the registry — the canonical 'what is NOT tested' location a reader and reviewer consult — does not carry it.
findings.required_correction: Add explicit entries to Appendix C's NOT-tested list for (i) increased Python expressivity beyond the tested operations, (ii) longer / more complex programs, (iii) generalization axes other than the four questions; and name program length/complexity at least once in ch25's widening note.
findings.acceptance_test: grep -i 'expressiv|longer|complex' book/manuscript/appendix_c_experiment_registry.md and ch25_conclusion.md returns at least one 'not tested' hit each, and each item is marked untested rather than 0.

findings.location: book/manuscript/appendix_c_experiment_registry.md:112, 145-154; grid rows at ch12:27, ch16:83, ch21:66, ch22:179; docs/experiments/stage4_composition.md:1-3, 62-67
findings.observed: The canonical 0.88M composition baseline (in-dist 0.900, composition 0.000) is not traceable to any manifest. Appendix C discloses that artifacts/manifests/stage4_composition.json is really the 29.3M run (verified: n_embd=448, 800 steps, 29,290,240 params, in-dist 0.8967) and that the baseline comes from evaluating stage1.pt on the composition split — but its registry row names no manifest, and the only manifest that evaluates stage1.pt on the composition split (artifacts/manifests/stage4_scaling.json, ckpt stage1.pt, pilot_tok, comp_per_op=40) records in-dist pass@1 = 0.9167 (n=60), not 0.900. Meanwhile docs/experiments/stage4_composition.md claims a 0.88M/1500-step run with in-dist 0.900 and cites artifacts/manifests/stage4_composition.json plus checkpoint stage4_composition.pt — both of which are the 29.3M artifacts (the .pt is 118 MB).
findings.evidence: stage4_composition.json config/model_params; stage4_scaling.json in_distribution MODEL pass_at_1 0.91666; ls artifacts/checkpoints/stage4_composition.pt = 118,002,858 bytes; docs/experiments/stage4_composition.md reproduce block.
findings.why_it_matters: The 0.88M composition baseline is one of the book's canonical values that review §1 requires to be traced across chapters; its headline in-distribution cell has no surviving manifest, the doc that documents it mis-cites the 29.3M manifest/checkpoint, and the nearest surviving re-evaluation disagrees (0.9167 vs 0.900).
findings.required_correction: Either locate and cite the manifest that recorded 0.900 for the 0.88M composition eval (stating its denominator), or restate the grid's 0.88M in-dist cell with the recorded value and denominator from stage4_scaling.json; and correct docs/experiments/stage4_composition.md to stop citing stage4_composition.json/.pt for a 0.88M run.
findings.acceptance_test: The 0.900 cell in ch12/ch16/ch21/ch22/Appendix C points to a named manifest whose recorded MODEL in-dist pass@1 equals the quoted value with a stated denominator, and docs/experiments/stage4_composition.md cites only 0.88M artifacts.

findings.observed: The registry row cites 'stage1.json / stage1.pt | in-dist 0.897', but artifacts/manifests/stage1.json records MODEL pass_at_1 = 0.0 (the pre-fix broken evaluation); the 0.897 figure lives in artifacts/manifests/stage1_results.json (0.89666). A reader following the registry's traceability promise lands on a manifest that contradicts the quoted number.
findings.evidence: stage1.json results[0] = {label MODEL, syntax_rate 0.0, pass_at_1 0.0}; stage1_results.json[0] pass_at_1 0.89666.
findings.why_it_matters: Appendix C is the book's single traceability index ('Every result in this book is traceable to a run ... where the numbers live'); pointing the canonical 0.897 at a manifest that records 0.000 breaks that promise and looks like a contradiction to any checking reader.
findings.required_correction: Cite stage1_results.json for the 0.897 result (and note that stage1.json preserves the pre-fix 0.000 evaluation referenced by Appendix B.1), or add a note in the row explaining the two manifests.
findings.acceptance_test: The Stage 1 registry row names a manifest whose recorded MODEL pass@1 equals 0.897, with the pre-fix 0.000 manifest explicitly identified where the failure ledger references it.

findings.observed: The experiment doc labels the canonical pilot pass@1 as 'problem-level pass@1 (deterministic/greedy) on the test set'. The book consistently states the opposite — temperature-0.8 single-sample multinomial decoding — and the code agrees with the book: src/model/gpt.py:110 def generate(..., temperature=0.8) with torch.multinomial at line 116.
findings.evidence: gpt.py:110-116; ch10:113-116; Appendix C decoding note; glossary 'Sampled decoding (what the book's numbers use)'.
findings.why_it_matters: Decoding protocol changes the meaning of every pass@1 in the book; a stale 'greedy' label in the experiment record contradicts the manuscript and would fail a reviewer's cross-check of the canonical 0.897.
findings.required_correction: Correct docs/experiments/stage1_pilot.md to 'temperature-0.8 single-sample sampled decoding' (book and code are authoritative); no manuscript change needed.
findings.acceptance_test: grep -i greedy docs/experiments/*.md returns no claim that any reported score used greedy/argmax decoding.

findings.observed: The doc's caveat says 'The joint model is trained on roughly twice the distinct examples and takes a longer training run' — contradicting ch20's one-variable claim that 'both protocols used the same example set and the same total step budget'. The script confirms the book: scripts/run_continual.py trains sequential with steps_a then steps_b and replay with allt = A_train + B_train for steps_a + steps_b (700+700 = 1400 for both, same A/B pools), and continual.json records one shared config.
findings.evidence: run_continual.py:72-86; continual.json config {steps_a 700, steps_b 700, n_per 70}; ch20:105-111.
findings.why_it_matters: The doc's statement, if believed, would invalidate the book's headline 'procedure, not data or budget' finding; the two records currently disagree on the central controlled variable of Chapter 18.
findings.required_correction: Rewrite the doc's cost caveat to state that both protocols used the same example pool and the same 700+700 step budget (only order/mixing differed), keeping only its valid points (joint is not a replay-after-A-first design; equal B acquisition is not zero cost).
findings.acceptance_test: docs/experiments/continual_learning.md no longer claims a larger or longer joint run; it states same pool and same total steps, matching run_continual.py and ch20.

findings.observed: The chapter's lesson reframes the Level-3 surface result as a species of Level-1 memorization: 'it escapes example-memorization but is caught by surface-memorization' and 'There are at least two kinds [of memorization], and they have very different implications.' This folds the Surface level into the Memorization level the taxonomy keeps as distinct questions (ch02:60-78), while ch22 and the glossary keep Q1 and Q3 as separate probes.
findings.evidence: ch02:60-78 defines Q1 Memorization and Q3 Surface as separate questions; ch22:100-105 insists the four are 'separate evaluations, not steps of a single ascending scale'; ch14:166-179 uses 'surface-memorization' as a kind of memorization.
findings.why_it_matters: Terminology that merges two of the four levels invites readers (and later summaries) to treat the surface collapse as a memorization result, eroding the never-collapse rule at exactly the chapter that introduces the distinction.
findings.required_correction: Rename the second kind (e.g. 'surface-tied association' / 'phrasing association') and keep 'memorization' for Q1, or add an explicit note that the book is extending the word while Q1 and Q3 remain separate measured questions.
findings.acceptance_test: ch14 no longer classifies the surface result as a kind of memorization without an explicit disambiguation that Q1 and Q3 stay separate.

findings.observed: The chapter introduces the Level-4 composition failure as 'the deep meaning of "surface-tied" that we began to glimpse in Chapter 15' — i.e. it glosses the structural result as an extension of the surface (L3) result — while the same chapter later insists the two numbers 'measure different kinds of capability' (lines 158-163) and the taxonomy requires them reported separately.
findings.evidence: ch16:135-143 vs ch16:158-163 and ch02:76-78 ('never mash these four into one number').
findings.why_it_matters: Presenting L4 as 'the deep meaning of' L3 merges two generalization levels into one explanatory claim, the exact collapse the book's framework forbids, and it sits in the chapter that is supposed to be the cleanest separation of the two.
findings.required_correction: Reframe the paragraph so the structural failure is not defined as a deeper instance of surface-tiedness: state the L4 observation on its own terms and label any shared-mechanism reading as an explicitly separate [INTERPRETATION]/[HYPOTHESIS] that was not tested.
findings.acceptance_test: The paragraph no longer glosses the composition result as 'the deep meaning of surface-tied'; L3 and L4 claims in ch16 are each scoped to their own measurement.

findings.observed: The conclusion's final takeaway blockquote opens unscoped: 'A small model learns narrow tasks well, but its knowledge is surface-tied and non-compositional; more capacity (0.88M→29.3M) does not change the compositional limit.' The first clause generalizes from one task family, one architecture family and one generator to 'a small model' with no tested-surface caveat, dropping the scoping ch22's opening requires ('These are claims about this brew, not universal laws about all small models').
findings.evidence: ch22:8-13 scoping paragraph; ch25:186-188 blockquote; only the capacity clause carries a range.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the sentence most likely to be quoted or indexed; as written it is a universal-sounding claim scoped only implicitly, and it also merges the surface and composition limits into one property of 'a small model' generally.
findings.required_correction: Scope the blockquote to the tested regime (e.g. 'The small model in this brew — 0.88M-29.3M decoder-only transformers on our NL-to-Python task — learns narrow tasks well; in our tests its knowledge was surface-tied and non-compositional').
findings.acceptance_test: The final blockquote names the tested model range, task and regime before asserting surface-tiedness and non-composition.

findings.observed: The chapter converts a single-seed coverage result into practice advice: 'a practitioner who cannot acquire more data can often get a large improvement just by diversifying the data they already have ... can turn a brittle 0.500/0.000 model into one that covers 1.000/1.000 of the tested surfaces — with zero additional data. That is the kind of result that changes how a dataset would actually be built.' The chapter's own caveat (lines 103-128) establishes the 1.000 is coverage of surfaces inside the training family, not transfer to an unseen family, from one run (diversity.json: steps 900, seed 0, n_train 1200).
findings.evidence: diversity.json single seed; ch13:103-128 coverage-not-generalization caveat; docs/experiments/diversity_vs_quantity.md 'the strong reading ... is not fully established by this design'.
findings.why_it_matters: A universal-sounding practitioner recommendation rests on a coverage-only, one-seed result on one synthetic surface; without the scope it reads as a general law of dataset construction.
findings.required_correction: Scope the recommendation to what was measured (one run, one task, coverage of surfaces within the tested family set) and restate that transfer to an unseen wording family was not demonstrated.
findings.acceptance_test: The practical-implication paragraph carries the coverage-only scope and the single-run/one-task scope in the same paragraph as the 1.000/1.000 claim.

findings.observed: The design doc still specifies eight acts and 23-24 chapters, including 'Act VI — Give It More Python (Ch18 capability expansion, Ch19 ladder revisited)' and Act VIII chapters, while the implemented manuscript is 7 parts / 21 chapters / 4 appendices with headings 1-21 and no capability-expansion chapters (ch25:164-177 states that sweep was not run).
findings.evidence: design/BOOK_DESIGN.md §9 vs manuscript headings (ch20 file = heading 18, ch21 = 19, ch22 = 20, ch25 = 21) and review/PUBLICATION_REVIEW_INSTRUCTIONS.md §1 structure list.
findings.why_it_matters: Review §4 requires disposing of this as a design/repo documentation reconciliation (option c) rather than inventing experiments; a stale spec promising absent content will keep regenerating 'missing chapter' findings every pass until it is updated.
findings.required_correction: Update design/BOOK_DESIGN.md §9 to the implemented 7-part/21-chapter structure with an explicit note that ability-ladder stages 5-6 (more Python, length/complexity) were folded into future work because no experiment measured them, cross-referencing ch25's widening note. Do not add experiments.
findings.acceptance_test: design/BOOK_DESIGN.md's act/chapter list matches the manuscript's 21 chapter headings + 4 appendices and flags the compressed stages as future work.

findings.observed: 'The model never produced a correct program for any composite operation it saw, even though every composite is a combination of primitives the aggregate shows it largely knows.' The composites were never seen (holdout by design), so 'it saw' contradicts the chapter's own setup three paragraphs earlier ('We never show it a held-out composite operation').
findings.why_it_matters: In the book's central negative-result paragraph the sentence as written asserts training exposure that did not happen — a factual contradiction a reviewer will read as either a design error or a drafting slip.
findings.required_correction: Change to 'any composite operation it was asked' / 'it never saw'.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence no longer says the model saw composite operations.
